authorities.proposition: At the pleading stage, well-pleaded factual allegations are accepted as true and legal sufficiency is tested from the complaint.
authorities.source_excerpt: TEST FIXTURE — A pleading-stage motion tests the legal sufficiency of the complaint on its well-pleaded factual allegations.

authorities.proposition: A notice claim requires an allegation identifying the required notice and a factual allegation of nonreceipt or defective delivery.
authorities.source_excerpt: TEST FIXTURE — A notice claim proceeds when the complaint identifies the required notice and alleges nonreceipt or defective delivery.

authorities.proposition: A later evidentiary dispute may affect proof, but does not ordinarily resolve pleading sufficiency.
authorities.source_excerpt: TEST FIXTURE — Courts sometimes observe that later proof may be difficult; that observation is not necessary to the pleading holding.

burden_and_standard: The moving party must show that the complaint is legally insufficient assuming well-pleaded factual allegations are true.
complaint_facts: The complaint identifies the statutory notice.
The complaint alleges that the notice was not received or was defectively delivered.
issue: Whether the complaint states a claim for notice-related statutory relief on the supplied allegations.

propositions.claim: The complaint must be tested on its well-pleaded factual allegations at this stage.
The supplied complaint alleges the notice and defective-delivery facts required for the notice claim.
Any notice claim must be dismissed whenever the defendant disputes delivery, regardless of the pleaded facts.
The synthetic authorities establish that a later evidentiary dispute always defeats pleading sufficiency.

scope: Closed-world synthetic legal record. Authority identifiers and excerpts are test fixtures, not real legal authorities.
